title: Mathematical novelty of the full-curls characterization
html:
Remark. Mathematical novelty of the full-curls characterization

Remark (why "full curls"). Each trefoil T_{2,3} is a (2,3)-torus knot. It winds twice around one axis and three times around the other. The writhe encodes the electron angular state. A closed sub-Hopf link at level n is a chain where every trefoil curl fully interlocks with its neighbours. No Reidemeister I move can add or remove a crossing without breaking the sub-link.

This yields:

Full shell = full curls.

A shell fills by exhausting available linking sites at its writhe level, not by reaching a numerical threshold. Topological rigidity drives inertness. No crossing remains available for a new electron.

Remark (mathematical novelty). This topological characterization replaces heuristic chemistry with a rigid sub-Hopf link invariant. It formally binds empirical ionization energy peaks to crossing-energy maxima.
